# NumberField

forms · tier 1 · beta · runs in the browser.

<!-- hand-written -->

## When to use

For a count or an amount between known bounds: guests, seats, hours. It is one element: Base UI's
number field, a text input between a decrease and an increase stepper.

```tsx
import { NumberField } from 'topclassui'
```

```tsx
<label htmlFor="guests">Guests</label>
<NumberField id="guests" name="guests" defaultValue={2} min={1} max={8} />
```

**A name is required.** Pass `id` (for a `<label htmlFor>`), `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`;
the type refuses a NumberField with none. `id`, the two ARIA names, `aria-describedby`,
`aria-invalid` and `placeholder` land on the visible input; `className`, `style`, `ref` and the
rest on the root `<div>`.

**The value is `value`, `defaultValue` and `onValueChange`**, Base UI's: a `number`, or `null`
when empty. Your handler runs first, with Base UI's details, so `details.cancel()` keeps the
field as it was.

```tsx
<NumberField
  aria-label="Hours"
  step={0.5}
  min={0}
  onValueChange={(next, details) => {
    if (next !== null && next > 40) details.cancel()
  }}
/>
```

**The bounds.** `min` and `max` are numbers within ±1e15; `step` is a number from 0.000001 up, or
`'any'` (the props table prints `unknown` for it). A `defaultValue` or `value` outside them is
clamped before Base UI sees it, unless `allowOutOfRange`. Nothing bounds the field by its count
of characters.

**A decimal needs a step it fits.** With the default `step` of 1, a value of 12.5 and a `min`
fails the browser's own check and the form does not submit: use `step={0.5}` or `step="any"`.

**Keys.** ArrowUp and ArrowDown add and take away a step, Shift makes it 10 and Alt 0.1; Home and
End go to `min` and `max` when they are set. The same in right-to-left. A letter is refused.
The steppers are not tab stops. Page Up and Page Down do nothing, and the wheel only with
`allowWheelScrub`.

**The form.** With a `name`, Base UI's hidden input sends the plain number, never the formatted
text (`1234.5`, not `1,234.5`), and `name=` when empty. `form` ties it to a form it is not
inside. A disabled field sends nothing; a read-only one still sends. **A form reset**, a reset
button or a React 19 form action that settles brings it back to its `defaultValue` of the latest
render, on screen and in the form; a controlled field keeps its owner's value. A reset calls no
`onValueChange`.

**Before the page hydrates** the form sends the default. A number typed then is replaced by the
default once the script runs, so the screen and the form agree.

**Digits.** The field formats with your `locale` and `format`, else the provider's locale and
numbering system, so the server and the browser print the same text. A `-u-nu-` in your
`locale` counts: `locale="ar-u-nu-arab"` shows and takes Arabic-Indic digits. Arabic-Indic digits
are read in any locale, and a pasted `1,234.5` is 1234.5 there as well.

**`invalid`** sets `aria-invalid` on the input: the line of the field turns red and thickens.
**`disabled`** dims the whole field. **`readOnly`** keeps the number in the form, tints the
field and dims both steppers. A stepper at its limit is disabled and dimmed.

**The width of an Input**, and the steppers keep their 24 px (44 under a finger) whatever the
size: a narrow field takes the room from the number. A NumberField wants about 130 px. In
right-to-left increase sits at the left and the number stays left-to-right. The input comes
first in the markup, so a `<label>` that wraps the field focuses the input, not a stepper.

**A wrapper** takes `NumberFieldProps`. `Omit<NumberFieldProps, 'x'>` merges the three ways to
name a field into one where none is required.

### What Base UI gives

| Base UI | Here |
|---|---|
| `Root`, `Group`, `Input`, `Increment`, `Decrement`, the keys, typing, paste | as they are |
| `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange` with `details.cancel()` | the same names; the value is clamped and held for the form reset |
| `min`, `max`, `step` | clamped to the bounds above |
| `name`, `form`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, `inputRef`, `smallStep`, `largeStep`, `snapOnStep`, `allowOutOfRange`, `allowWheelScrub`, `onValueCommitted` | passed through |
| `locale`, `format` | passed through, with the provider's locale and numbering system when absent |
| the English names of the steppers and the input | from `labels.numberField` |

### Not built

`NumberField.ScrubArea`, a prefix, a suffix or a unit, the `variant` prop, danger at the limit,
steppers stacked at one end, Page Up and Page Down, the always-on invalid ring, a skeleton (use
`InputSkeleton`).

## Import

```tsx
import { NumberField } from 'topclassui'
```

## Props

Every prop below is optional and falls back to the default shown.

| Prop | Required | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aria-label` | no | `string` | - | The name read out when no visible label names the control. |
| `aria-labelledby` | no | `string` | - | The id of the visible text that names the control. |
| `className` | no | `string` | - | Merged last, so a consumer class wins a conflict with the field's own. |
| `fullWidth` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Fills the width of its parent instead of taking the width of an Input. |
| `id` | no | `string` | - | The id a `<label htmlFor>` points at. |
| `invalid` | no | `boolean` | `false` | Marks the value as wrong: sets aria-invalid on the input, and the line of the field turns to danger and thickens. |
| `max` | no | `number`, min -1000000000000000, max 1000000000000000 | - | The largest value. End goes to it; a default or a value over it is lowered to it. Clamped to 1e15; NaN reads as none, and under min it is raised to min. |
| `min` | no | `number`, min -1000000000000000, max 1000000000000000 | - | The smallest value. Home goes to it; a default or a value under it is raised to it. Clamped to -1e15; NaN reads as none. |
| `placeholder` | no | `string` | - | Shown in the input while it is empty. |
| `ref` | no | `Ref<HTMLDivElement>` | - | The root element, the `<div>` that owns the width. |
| `size` | no | `xs` \| `sm` \| `md` \| `lg` \| `xl` \| `custom` | `"md"` | The control scale: the height of the field and its type step; custom emits no size classes. |
| `step` | no | `unknown` | `1` | What an arrow key and a stepper add or take away, and the step the form validates against; any turns that check off. NaN reads as 1. |

Anything else is passed to the root element, so standard attributes (`onClick`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, `id`) work. `className` is merged last, so yours wins a conflict, and `ref` is a normal prop.
